description: Wrangl: Agent Hierarchy — SessionStart injects the resolved role→model table and the orchestration protocol on startup, resume, clear, fork, and post-compaction (so it survives compaction). It classifies the session three ways: a subagent (agent_id set) gets nothing, which is the intent here, since role agents carry their own instructions in agents/*.md and an Implementor that starts orchestrating would defeat the hierarchy; a top-level `claude --agent <hierarchy role>` session that a team claims gets a short notice that it is NOT the Orchestrator; a session that is in (flagged by /wrangl:orchestrator or by an ah2 act of its own, owning a team, or under alwaysOrchestrator) gets the ordinary directive; everything else stays bare, with no output from any hook that talks to the model. PostToolUse on Skill|Bash, PostToolUseFailure on Bash and UserPromptSubmit opt a session in on an ah2 command or skill, or an ah call that leaves it owning a team; any other ah call leaves it bare. Every unit but the ways in does nothing for a session that is not part of ah, and a deny needs a positively identified session: no binary, a refused home, an unknown unit, unusable input, or a failure while identifying passes the call with one hook-errors row. The discriminator is agent_id, not agent_type — a top-level --agent session sets agent_type too, so testing it misclassifies a genuine main session as a subagent. Silent when the config sets enabled:false; with no config at all a session that is in gets a one-line nudge to run /hierarchy init. PreToolUse runs one process, ah-hook pretooluse-chain, which runs every gate whose matcher fits the tool. There is no Ultra-Advisor gate: `ah gate` only prints a removal notice. SubagentStop runs the usage collector: it sums the finished subagent's transcript (token counts the harness already logged) into ~/.claude/ah2/agent-hierarchy.usage.jsonl — plain code, zero model cost — which /hierarchy usage or ah usage-report renders as session/day/week/month reports. UserPromptSubmit also tracks the peer report-back contract: a delivered prompt carrying a `[hierarchy-peer-brief reply-to="..." task="..."]` sentinel inside its `<cross-session-message>` wrapper records a pending obligation in ~/.claude/ah2/agent-hierarchy.peer-pending.jsonl. PostToolUse (matcher SendMessage) resolves that obligation once a reply is sent to the recorded address, its name, or an explicit third-party reply-to. Stop blocks the session's turn from ending while an obligation is still owed, nudging at most twice before waiving it and allowing the stop regardless — fail-open throughout, and inert for subagents, exactly like the other hooks above. Enforcement arms only on a peer-delivered turn: UserPromptSubmit also arms a per-session turn marker whenever a wrapped message (a brief, a ping, or anything else carrying the cross-session-message envelope) leaves a pending obligation behind, and Stop's nudge/waive logic runs only on an armed turn, disarming it afterward either way — so a user directly chatting with a tasked peer neither triggers a nudge nor spends one. Two more mechanisms, both fail-open and inert for subagents. Message files: PreToolUse on SendMessage (ah-hook pretooluse-msg-gate) records a bare send after it is sent (PostToolUse): a follow-up links to the open request, other sends become a request whose clock arms when the member works; never denies; SubagentStop runs the response nudge — a hierarchy role subagent briefed by file whose final message lacks `[hierarchy-msg <response path>]` is blocked ONCE (per agent_id, recorded in gates.jsonl) with instructions to write its response file; the peer-side resolver likewise requires the response pointer when the obligation was recorded with one. Peer roster: a top-level `--agent <role>` session appends `up` at SessionStart and `down` at SessionEnd (ah-hook sessionend-roster) to `<hierarchy dir>/peers.jsonl`; PostToolUse on ListAgents|SendMessage (ah-hook posttooluse-roster) records `seen` (parsed from the ListAgents listing, role-matching names only) and `briefed`; SessionStart appends a HIERARCHY STATE block (open exchanges, roster, tier line) on every matcher including compact, and sweeps closed exchanges older than 7 days on startup. `msgs:"off"` in agent-hierarchy.json disables the two message gates; the CLI and the state listing stay. Streams: ah-hook stream-label runs on UserPromptSubmit, Stop and Notification (matcher permission_prompt) only in a roster-spawned herdr peer whose team row is tagged into an open stream, and re-renders that stream's tab glyph through `ah roster stream-label`, the same CLI that holds the other stream verbs (`stream-open`, `stream-status`, `stream-done`) and `--stream` on `spawn-one`/`spawn-ad-hoc`. ah blocks no push or merge; it records them, and "do not push" is an instruction in a member's brief. PostToolUse on Bash (ah-hook posttooluse-merge-record) appends a merge line to the run's decision log when the pinned merge command of a /pipeline run ran. The activity hook (ah-hook activity) records a Claude role session's own activity for the hierarchy status file: UserPromptSubmit working, Stop idle, a permission prompt or an AskUserQuestion blocked, and PostToolUse (async) working again; UserPromptSubmit and Stop also refresh status.json in a session that is part of ah.
registry: The one registry of Wrangl's hook rows, read by hooks/register.ts (the mod that runs each row through bin/ah-hook on the mod event below) and by every test that checks the wiring. `hooks` keeps the classic shape: one command per row, the same matchers, the same order within an event. `mod` names the mod event each classic event runs on.
